title: Learning Macroscopic Dynamics without Reconstructing Microscopic States
abstract: arXiv:2609.37392v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modeling the temporal evolution of macroscopic properties of complex systems is an important scientific task. To predict this evolution without full microscopic simulation, a common approach encodes microstates into compact latent states, learns their evolution, and reads out macroscopic predictions from the latent trajectory. These latent states are often learned through microstate reconstruction. However, with limited latent capacity, reconstruction can favor high-variance microscopic details over information needed for macroscopic prediction. Yet jointly learning latent states and their transition without reconstruction often fails to obtain latent dynamics that support accurate macroscopic prediction. We show that this failure can arise from latent scale collapse: shrinking the latent state scale reduces training loss while macroscopic evolution error remains large. translated_title: 无需重构微观状态的宏观动力学学习
translated_abstract: 对复杂系统宏观性质的时间演化进行建模是一项重要的科学任务。为了在不进行完整微观模拟的情况下预测这种演化，一种常见方法是将微观状态编码为紧凑的潜在状态，学习其演化过程，并从潜在轨迹中读出宏观预测。这些潜在状态通常通过微观状态重构来学习。然而，在潜在容量有限的情况下，重构可能更偏向高方差的微观细节，而非宏观预测所需的信息。但如果不进行重构而联合学习潜在状态及其转移，又往往无法获得能够支持准确宏观预测的潜在动力学。我们证明，这种失败可能源于潜在尺度坍缩：缩小潜在状态的尺度虽然会降低训练损失，但宏观演化误差仍然很大。在此，我们提出了一个无需重构的框架来学习潜在状态……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了一种“潜在尺度坍缩”失败机制，并据此提出一个无需重构微观状态的框架，能够直接学习支持准确宏观预测的潜在动力学。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies "latent scale collapse" as a key failure mechanism and proposes a reconstruction-free framework that directly learns latent dynamics supporting accurate macroscopic prediction.
